releaseNotes:
Infra 0.11.1 — a click answers at once. Nothing new leaves your instance: the update check is unchanged (version + installation ID), and so is consented feedback escalation. No schema change.

FIXES. Clicking a link now shows right away that it worked: a bar across the top, the destination lit in the sidebar, and the page dimmed if the wait lasts. Before, nothing changed until the next page was ready, which invited more clicks, and each one started the page over. A repeat click on a link already loading is ignored; a different link still goes there. The same bar shows when you change a list's search, filters, page or saved view, and the search box keeps your place while you type. Saving a view can no longer be sent twice by a double click. The dashboard's Waiting on you loads faster when many items await approval.

UPGRADING. Change the image tag to 0.11.1. No migration and nothing to do by hand. If you are still on 0.10.1, this also applies everything in 0.11.0, including its migration: read the 0.11.0 notes first, for what the Warranty Claim template needs and the limits on rolling back to 0.10.1.

history.releaseNotes:
Infra 0.11.1 — a click answers at once. Nothing new leaves your instance: the update check is unchanged (version + installation ID), and so is consented feedback escalation. No schema change.

FIXES. Clicking a link now shows right away that it worked: a bar across the top, the destination lit in the sidebar, and the page dimmed if the wait lasts. Before, nothing changed until the next page was ready, which invited more clicks, and each one started the page over. A repeat click on a link already loading is ignored; a different link still goes there. The same bar shows when you change a list's search, filters, page or saved view, and the search box keeps your place while you type. Saving a view can no longer be sent twice by a double click. The dashboard's Waiting on you loads faster when many items await approval.

UPGRADING. Change the image tag to 0.11.1. No migration and nothing to do by hand. If you are still on 0.10.1, this also applies everything in 0.11.0, including its migration: read the 0.11.0 notes first, for what the Warranty Claim template needs and the limits on rolling back to 0.10.1.

Infra 0.11.0 — real claims, correctable stages, one place for fields. From Round 6. Nothing new leaves your instance: the update check is unchanged (version + installation ID), and so is consented feedback escalation. The new read API routes answer your own API keys and users; they send nothing anywhere. One migration applies at start. Nothing to do by hand.

FIXES THAT PROTECT DATA. Redoing a stage no longer loses its old answers: every replaced answer is in History, old to new. Answers replaced before 0.11.0 cannot be recovered. Deactivating a custom field no longer erases its values on the next save; they stay, read-only, as "No longer asked". Values already erased cannot be recovered. A column named changeDescription now reaches its own field instead of overwriting Change Notes (R6-09). A duplicate version number never creates a second version. History no longer drops an owner change between two people outside your role's view.

SEVERAL PRODUCTS ON ONE CLAIM. A stage can carry line items, one row per product, filled across stages, with partial results per product. A row whose quantities do not add up warns and never blocks. Rows show on the Workflow tab and printed record, the type's tab filters on them, and /api/export/eventLines gives one row per product.

CORRECTING A STAGE. Any completed stage can be edited in any order: Update needs no reason, Correction does, History shows old to new. Edit replaces Reopen. Changing a gate's answer clears nothing, and the screen shows the effect before you save. An edited approved stage goes back for approval.

FIELDS (PROPERTIES). Settings → Fields lists every field of every record type: standard and custom, who made it, where it is used, how many records hold a value. Custom Fields moved here. Shared lists hold long sets of values such as products and customers, with type to search and one level of parent, kept up on screen or by CSV. A field can change type once it holds values, through a checked conversion that previews first and records each change in History. A conversion that changes the text on an approved stage sends it back for approval, and a completed event returns to Open.

WARRANTY CLAIM. The shipped template reflects your practice claim, but your copy does not change on upgrade. Open the type and compare stage by stage to adopt what you choose, or Reset it. Product ships as free text. To choose it from a list, populate the list and convert the column under Fields, after any Reset: a Reset removes list pointers, while adopting keeps them.

ALSO. Watching a type shows its completed events and alerts on the dashboard, without being a step. Corrections to versions already imported: provenance and attachments by import, with a reason and re-authentication. Add a file to an approved version as a recorded correction. Marking a document reviewed moves its review dates, so the overdue alert clears (S-09). Outline numbering in the editor. Impact Review can be turned off per template. Event type defaults appear when you pick the type. Saving with no changes writes nothing. A printable flow overview, a next number for continuing a sequence, History filters. Read API: eventStages, eventLines, history, listEntries; API keys remain read-only. The upgrade command on Settings needs no editing (E-63). Entering today's date in the evening no longer warns that it is before the event was opened.

UPGRADING. Change the image tag to 0.11.0. Rolling back to 0.10.1 is an image swap, with limits: line items are ignored there, and completing an active stage loses that stage's line values; saving an event type there drops its line items, list pointers and "added by", so avoid editing types while rolled back; list-backed fields read as free text; custom fields erase retired values on save again; the watching card disappears; converted values stay converted.

Infra 0.10.1 — true dashboard counts, a reset that keeps hand-offs. Answers PUB-2026-0017. Nothing new leaves your instance: the update check is unchanged (version + installation ID), and so is consented feedback escalation. No schema change.

FIXES. Dashboard items count every match (they stopped at 50); the list still previews 50. Archived documents leave the "differs from its template" check everywhere. Your question: applying a template's Approval required setting on 0.10.0 did change Archived documents too, each change in that document's History; from 0.10.1 it does not. Reset to shipped definition keeps each stage's Handled by, due days and approval where the stage still exists, and previews what is kept or lost first. If you already reset a type on 0.10.0, set those again by hand. Old "Owner changed" entries with no owner change read "Updated"; notes and reviews no longer say "Reason:". Dark mode: dropdowns and multi-line text boxes are dark.

READ API AND AI PROFILE. The AI Instance Profile describes each stage in full (handler, due days, approval with names, fields, decision options, task items). The events export takes a type by name (view=Warranty Claim).

FEEDBACK AND LAYOUT (PUB-2026-0017). One Feedback button with a 3-second countdown (click again to capture now, Escape to cancel; Ctrl+Shift+F is instant). Editors and settings pages use the width of a laptop screen.

ALSO IN 0.10.0, MISSING FROM ITS NOTES. Links to other websites in document content open in a new tab (record links stay put); the editor toolbar stays in view on long documents.

YOUR QUESTION. A stage whose handler depends on an earlier answer: set Handled by to a role holding both people; the owner can reassign the stage on a single claim. No change planned.

UPGRADING. Change the image tag to 0.10.1. No migration, nothing else to run. Rolling back to 0.10.0 is a plain image swap.

Infra 0.10.0 — document control you can show an auditor. Answers PUB-2026-0012 to PUB-2026-0016. Nothing new leaves your instance: the update check is unchanged (version + installation ID), and so is consented feedback escalation. No schema change.

FIND RECORDS BY ID. Search matches display IDs, partly and in any case, on every list and in every record picker: "sop" lists every SOP.

VERSION CONTROL. Compare any two versions with headings, lists and tables kept and changed words marked. The change notes of every version in the range, with author, reviewers, approvers and change control. Open any version read-only (Effective, Superseded with its date, or Draft) and print it with the uncontrolled-copy footer. The version in force on Overview, with its effective date and original author. Version and Effective date as optional list columns.

APPROVALS. Turning Approval required on in a template can now be applied to its existing documents, each change recorded in History; a dashboard item lists documents that differ from their template. Signing to approve a document can be turned off even when no approvers are named.

READABLE HISTORY. Field names as on the form, names instead of IDs, dates instead of timestamps, system values hidden, for existing entries too (translated when shown, never rewritten). The audit-log export adds readable columns. Saving no longer logs an owner change when the owner did not change.

EVENTS. The shipped Warranty Claim follows the standard return flow (warranty check, return received, inspection finding, decision, Resolution); every claim ends in Resolution with the date the customer was told, and a rejection skips there and becomes the outcome. It reaches your instance only when you choose Reset on that type. Decision answers can skip ahead and record a result. List fields (customer, product, serial or lot, order) are columns, filters and export columns on a type's tab. Answers under a removed field still show. Document Impact Review covers linked documents, names each owner, and Mark reviewed ticks its line.

MORE. Review Log of every Mark reviewed, with export. One Users & Roles page; invites can name a role; the employee record shows the role. The map hides add-ins by default and draws their integrations from the parent, marked via. Ctrl+Shift+F captures feedback with a dropdown open; the Feedback list shows publisher references.

FIXED. A role that hides cost amounts or employee details could read them in History. A document's versions and attachments, an event's checklist and printed record, an integration's data fields and a record's history now follow the record's read scope.

UPGRADING. Pull and restart: no migration, nothing to run by hand. Rolling back to 0.9.0 is safe; an event type using "then go to" opens the next stage instead, and an invite made on 0.10.0 but accepted on 0.9.0 creates a read-only user.

Infra 0.9.0 — roles, approvals, and findings you can close. Answers PUB-2026-0011. Nothing new leaves your instance: the update check is unchanged (version + installation ID), and so is consented feedback escalation. Notes, reviews, roles and approvals stay on your instance.

ROLES. Named roles (Settings > Roles & Permissions): View, Create, Edit and Archive per record type — none, in scope, or all — plus Import and Export; approving documents is its own right. Scope is the records a person owns or is assigned, chosen departments, or records linked to chosen systems, and it limits what they see as well as what they change — lists, record pages, search, exports, map, dashboard and quiz agree. Cost amounts and employee details can be hidden from a role, removed by the server. The sidebar names the role; module grants became roles automatically.

APPROVALS AND HAND-OFFS. A workflow stage can need approval (people or roles, all required) before the next opens; self-approval is allowed unless the stage forbids it, and is labelled. Approving asks for your password or a recent single sign-on. Send back to this or an earlier stage, which reopens with what was entered. Stages can be assigned and handed off, and fall due a set number of days later. Documents use the same approvals, and Approval required is now enforced. Waiting on you on the dashboard.

EVENTS. Creator owns new events; event types set default owner, backup, governing document, follow-up days and a title template. Follow-up dates (past due shows red). Notes on every record. Events list tabs per type, suggestions apart, saved views. Renumber an event into its type's prefix; the old number still finds it.

FINDINGS YOU CAN CLOSE. Cost Review suggestions are retired: a cost that needs a field filled is a dashboard item linking straight to it. Mark reviewed on any record, with what you checked. Resolve a finding in one form across its costs, systems and vendors. Preview linked records in place. New checks: systems with no owner, costs not linked to a system, mission-critical systems with no employee admin, too many admins, events past due.

COSTS. Current rate vs latest charge; clear auto-renew. Paid through (a second vendor who is paid). Estimated charges. Prepaid blocks with a balance and a low-balance warning. One invoice's lines across costs, checked against its total. Cost center on each charge, in import, export, filters and year over year. License cost and vendor annual cost worked out from costs.

IMPORTS AND EXPORTS. Charges update by import by id; correction batches recorded as corrections with reasons. New columns for auto-renew, paid through, cost center, prepaid, estimated, usage and follow-up dates; notes and reviews in the read API. The AI Instance Profile starts with what is new.

SMALLER THINGS. Supported by and administered by on systems (new administers link); offboarding lists admin rights first. Clearer shipped type descriptions. Worth filling in on systems and employees. Map saved views on the server. Security: Next.js 15.5.28 (critical image-optimizer advisory) and sanitize-html 2.18.1.

UPGRADING. Pull and restart — nothing to run by hand. Two additive migrations; module grants become roles (grants kept); open Cost Review suggestions dismissed. Rolling back to 0.8.0 is safe for your data, but: read scope and hidden fields stop applying and people given a role after the upgrade become read only; a stage awaiting approval can be completed without it; document approvers are not enforced; prepaid usage entries look like hours bought. Back up before upgrading. Behaviour changes: a document that requires approval cannot be approved by editing its status; approving is a right of its own; Cost Review suggestions are no longer created.

Infra 0.8.0 — documents with pictures, imports you can trace. Nothing new leaves your instance: the update check is unchanged (version + installation ID); this registry now lists, per release, the escalation references it fixed, which your instance reads to mark escalated feedback Fixed. API keys stay read-only.

FIXES TO NUMBERS YOU ALREADY HAVE. Year over year compares costs charged in both years and names the rest; it is withheld when either year has fewer months of data; pace follows each cost's cadence. The cost duplicate check compared names wrongly. Duplicate Cost Review suggestions from before 0.7.0 are dismissed. JSON exports give date-only fields as dates.

DOCUMENTS. Images in bodies and files attached to versions, imported from an assets/ folder in an import set. Who wrote, reviewed and approved each version, with change control and sources. An import can make a version the pending revision or, where approval is not required, effective.

IMPORTS. Import history (also by API). Update files inside a set. Set files recognised by part of their name; none skipped silently. A ticked duplicate is imported. Invoice references separate same-day charges; near-date repeats are flagged; month-only charges. Previews name records and show dates as dates.

COSTS. Ended costs; costs that stopped charging, with their paid-through date set as Contract End in one step; a cost's own history; charge changes in History.

SMALLER THINGS. Escalated feedback shows Fixed in and can be closed. Release notes in Version history. Owner Attention flags on links; Decision event type; new link labels. Read API paging, updatedSince, in-body links, text search. sanitize-html 2.18.0.

UPGRADING. Pull and restart — nothing to run by hand. One additive migration (rollback-safe); duplicate suggestions dismissed; new shipped types and labels added. Local-disk storage: document files now live in the uploads volume — back it up. Behaviour change: costs past their Contract End are hidden from the Costs list by default.

Infra 0.7.1 — fixes. No schema change; nothing new leaves your instance.

- Settings & Branding opens again. On 0.7.0 the page failed with "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred". The sign-in method control loaded server-only code that a 0.7.0 change made fail in the browser. The build now checks that no page can do this again.

UPGRADING. Change the image tag to 0.7.1. No migrations, nothing else to run.

Infra 0.7.0 — October 2026. Billing you can see and trust. Nothing new leaves your instance: the new exports are read by your own key or browser, and the update check is unchanged.

FIXES TO NUMBERS AND DATES YOU ALREADY HAVE. Spend could silently undercount: a cost counted its own amount until it had any billing instance, then only its instances, so its first charge could drop out of every total. Every charge is now a billing instance — a new cost records the charge it was created with as its first one, and its own amount is its current rate. Existing data is not rewritten; an insight lists the costs whose own charge was never recorded. Amounts were stored with floating-point noise (93.6 as 93.59999999999999) from every screen and import; new amounts are stored exactly and the upgrade corrects older ones. Dates showed a day early west of Greenwich; they now show the date entered, in every time zone.

BILLING HISTORY. The Billing tab groups charges by fiscal year and month. Year over year compares this year to date with the same months last year, shows last year's total and where this year is heading, and says so instead of a percentage when last year has fewer months of data. A new Year over year page lines every fiscal year up by month, by cost type, vendor or person. Charges worth a look: after the contract ended or the system was decommissioned, several in a month, or well above the cost's own history. One Cost Review suggestion per cost.

A READ API YOU CAN FIND. GET /api/export lists every read endpoint; new exports for billing instances, document versions and entity links import back unchanged. The AI Instance Profile states its version and when a saved copy is stale.

MATCHING STATEMENTS. Vendors have Also appears as (DNH*GODADDY), employees Also known as (the name on their card); imports match them exactly and the AI profile lists them. The import preview warns on a charge already recorded or repeated in the file.

PEOPLE AND ACCESS. A has access to label for who uses a system. Marking someone as having left suggests an offboarding event listing their recorded access, assigned costs and owned records. Decommissioned, former vendors and former employees are hidden by default on their lists.

DOCUMENTS. Revising an approved document no longer replaces it: the approved version stays in force and is what readers see, and the draft is a revision beside it with its own Submit, Approve and Reject; approving it makes the next whole version. approved versions carry the drafts' change notes; history folds drafts and marks older approved versions Superseded; Last Reviewed is saved on create; Compare keeps spaces.

SMALLER THINGS. Event descriptions. Costs search vendor and assignee. Pickers accept a pasted display ID. The import wizard asks what the file is before taking it and maps a changeReason column. Invite links need an email and create one account. The update notice shows the exact command for your platform. Keyboard-friendly record tabs. Framework security update (next 15.5.27).

UPGRADING. Pull and restart — nothing to run by hand. Two additive migrations run on boot (an older image ignores the new columns); stored amounts with float noise are corrected; approved documents that were showing a draft show their approved version again, with the draft kept as a pending revision; new shipped types and labels (has access to) arrive add-only. Behaviour changes: a new cost creates its first billing instance; invites need an email; lists hide retired records until you tick Show; a draft on an approved document is a revision until approved.

Infra 0.6.1 — fixes. No schema change; nothing new leaves your instance.

- "Sync shipped defaults" no longer overwrites your edits. It reset every shipped event type (CAPA, Warranty Claim, Nonconformance…) to its shipped definition each time it ran. The button is now "Add new shipped types": it adds what you do not have and never changes existing types. To put one shipped type back, use "Reset to shipped definition" in its editor; fields you added are kept.
- The version history now starts with the version you installed (new instances; earlier ones keep their history as is).
- The reported version no longer depends on an environment variable outside release images.

UPGRADING. Pull and restart. No migrations.

Infra 0.6.0 — September 2026

Shaped by the first real instance. Two fixes protect data you already have, imports can now update as well as create, and a change to what a bug report can carry comes first.

WHAT LEAVES YOUR INSTANCE — bug escalation. The reporter's attachment can now be sent, as an explicit choice like the screenshot, without its file name; until now the review screen said "Attachment: Included" but the file never left. Your triage notes can go with a report, as a separate switch. The "never sent" box now names its exception: a screenshot, attachment or text you wrote carries what is in it, so each is shown in full and can be switched off. Choosing Escalated opens the review screen; a report can no longer read Escalated without being sent. Outbound requests shows your time zone and says which update checks were automatic.

DATA-PROTECTING FIXES. Removing or renaming an event-type field silently erased recorded answers on the next save; answered fields are now retired, not deleted. Invite links pointed at localhost behind a reverse proxy; they use the public address. Simultaneous creates could be given the same ID and fail; numbering is now serialised.

IMPORT. Update existing records by display ID, with an old-to-new preview, updates vs corrections, and a choice on blank cells. Import a whole set as one .zip or .xlsx: ordered, previewed together, rows may point at records the set creates. The file format, templates and the AI Instance Profile are on the Import tab. Document history backfills below the live version.

UNKNOWNS. New systems start Not assessed yet and new integrations Not known yet, instead of Low and Manual. Systems record when they were decommissioned; costs can renew every <month>; vendor roles (resold by, managed by, implemented by, supported by).

MAP. Unconnected systems go to a tray, relationship links draw as a layer, add-in connectors show by default, a status filter, and the legend is on the map.

GETTING STARTED. A two-minute tour with a made-up company replaces demo data — and with it the one place Infra hard-deleted records.

SMALLER THINGS. Nonconformance (NCR) and Needs Review event types; a supplier-qualification field set; billing templates; departed-owner flag; local timestamps; feedback fixes; grouped import warnings; cost exports include contract dates; both critical dependency advisories fixed.

UPGRADING. Pull and restart; two additive migrations run on boot. Run Sync shipped defaults to receive the new event types and labels — it resets edits to shipped types, never your own. Rollback caveat: a system Not assessed yet, or an integration Not known yet, cannot be read by 0.5.x.

Infra 0.5.0, September 2026

Single sign-on, a deliberate visual identity with a dark theme, and exports you can scope.

SINGLE SIGN-ON (Microsoft Entra ID), optional. Register Infra with your directory and sign in with a Microsoft account, and optionally turn the password form off so your MFA and conditional-access policies apply to every sign-in. With no provider configured nothing changes at all.
  - Signing in does not create accounts: an active Infra user with the same email must already exist. Authenticating proves who someone is; it does not decide whether they may use this instance. It also keeps your user list truthful, since deactivating someone here is what raises the events for reassigning their records and equipment.
  - There is no break-glass password account. Recovering from a broken provider always happens at the infrastructure layer (fix the directory, update the variable, restart), so a standing local password would shorten nothing. If the provider variables are removed, the instance falls back to email and password automatically.

WHAT LEAVES YOUR INSTANCE: one addition. If, and only if, you enable single sign-on, your instance exchanges an authorisation code with the provider you configured each time someone signs in. It goes there and nowhere else and carries no record data. Two honest notes: it does NOT appear under Settings > Outbound requests, because that log covers requests Infra makes itself rather than ones the authentication library makes on your behalf; and Infra calls your provider for nothing else: no directory queries, no profile photos, no group lookups, no background sync. This release specifically removed a profile-photo request the library made by default.

DESIGN. The interface was assembled from framework defaults over a dozen build sessions and had started to look it. It has been replaced with a considered design, and dark mode, promised by a setting since 0.3.0, now actually works, with a per-browser toggle. Printing always uses the light theme. Your brand colours still drive the accent, and there is now a reset control and a typable hex field.

SCOPED EXPORT. Every directory gained an Export CSV button that carries the filters you have applied, so what is on screen is what downloads. You can also export only the records linked to another record (every event associated with SYS-1, for instance).

SMALLER THINGS. Vendors can be typed Government Agency or Certification Body. Cost duplicate detection now normalises dash variants, spacing and case, uses vendor to discriminate, and warns about a same-vendor same-day same-amount charge described differently. Dashboard lists share one format and renewals are no longer reported twice. "Report Bug" is now "Feedback".

UPGRADING. Pull and restart; migrations run on boot. Two additive migrations. One rollback caveat: a vendor tagged Government Agency or Certification Body cannot be read by 0.4.0, because adding a value to a fixed list is not as reversible as adding a column. Nothing else in this release has that property.

This release changes what an Infra instance sends out, so those items come first.

- The update check now sends two things and nothing else: the version you are running, and a random installation ID your instance generated for itself. No company name, no hostname, no user or record data. The ID exists so real installations can be counted and supported; it means nothing outside the publisher's registry, and your instance shows it to you.
- Bug reports you escalate carry a DIFFERENT, independently generated ID. Neither is derived from the other, so "this installation is still running" cannot be matched against "this installation reported a bug". Both IDs are visible in your own settings, and linking them is something only you can choose to do.
- Every outbound request is now written to your own log before it is sent. A new page, Settings → Outbound requests, lists every request Infra has ever made, with the full URL as sent and whether it succeeded. If the log entry cannot be written, the request is not sent.
- Update checks moved from daily to weekly, and now run for any signed-in user rather than only a SuperAdmin, so an instance with few admins is not mistaken for an abandoned one.
- Update checks now go to the publisher's own registry rather than to GitHub. The file published is the same one.
- New: send a bug report to the publisher, with a review screen first. A SuperAdmin can escalate one specific report. Before anything leaves, the screen shows the exact payload, including the screenshot, which can be removed with one click, and your instance's record counts, which can be withheld. Nothing is ever sent automatically, in bulk, or in the background, and a report is sent once.
- Turn the update check off at any time by clearing the update URL in Admin Settings or unsetting VERSION_CHECK_URL. You then stop being told when a fix ships; nothing else changes.

- Easier self-hosting: Infra now ships as a prebuilt container image with a complete step-by-step setup guide: download, set two values, and run.
- Navigation & UX polish: breadcrumbs on every detail and form page, a reorganized Settings hub, and a single unified "Add" action for linked records.
- Automatic updates: instances now record their version automatically on deploy (no manual step), and admins see an update banner with release notes and a download link.
- Security & platform: upgraded the underlying application framework and cleared all high-severity dependency advisories.
- Cloud storage: added Azure Blob Storage as a durable file-storage option for cloud and multi-host deployments.
- Initial published container image and the first release recorded in the registry.
